name: percpu_array_map_gen_lookup
prose: Precondition: map is a valid percpu array map and insn_buf points to a writable array of at least 10 struct bpf_insn entries. Postcondition: the function returns -EOPNOTSUPP without writing to insn_buf if bpf_jit_supports_percpu_insn() is false or if map->map_flags has BPF_F_INNER_MAP set; otherwise it writes 10 instructions into insn_buf (9 when map->bypass_spec_v1 is set) and returns the number of instructions written, and the caller retains ownership of insn_buf.
note: Checked arraymap.c:265-294: -EOPNOTSUPP at 271/274, insn count 10 (or 9 when bypass_spec_v1, lines 280-285) returned as insn - insn_buf. Prose correct, kept.

name: bpf_percpu_array_copy
prose: Precondition: key points to a readable u32 index and value points to a writable buffer of at least nr_possible_cpus * array->elem_size bytes. Postcondition: the function returns -ENOENT without taking the RCU read lock or modifying value if the index is >= map->max_entries; otherwise it takes the RCU read lock, copies each possible CPU's value into value at offsets 0, array->elem_size, 2*array->elem_size, ... for each possible CPU, initializes map fields in each copied slot, releases the RCU read lock, and returns 0, with the caller retaining ownership of all buffers.
note: Checked arraymap.c:310-335: -ENOENT before rcu_read_lock (318-319), per-CPU copy_map_value_long + check_and_init_map_value, returns 0. Prose correct, kept.

name: array_map_get_next_key
prose: Precondition: next_key points to a writable u32 and key is either NULL or points to a readable u32 index. Postcondition: the function writes 0 to *next_key and returns 0 when key is NULL or the index is >= map->max_entries, returns -ENOENT without writing to *next_key when the index equals map->max_entries - 1, and otherwise writes index + 1 to *next_key and returns 0; the caller retains ownership of all buffers.
note: Checked arraymap.c:338-354: key NULL gives index U32_MAX so *next = 0; index >= max_entries gives 0; index == max_entries-1 gives -ENOENT without writing; else index+1. Prose correct, kept.

name: array_map_update_elem
prose: Precondition: key points to a readable u32 index and value points to a readable value of map's value size. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if (map_flags & ~BPF_F_LOCK) > BPF_EXIST, otherwise -E2BIG if the index is >= map->max_entries, otherwise -EEXIST if BPF_NOEXIST is set, otherwise -EINVAL if BPF_F_LOCK is set and map->record lacks BPF_SPIN_LOCK, and in each of these error cases leaves the map unchanged; otherwise it copies value into the element slot (for a percpu array map into the current CPU's percpu area using copy_map_value; for other maps using copy_map_value_locked when BPF_F_LOCK is set and copy_map_value otherwise), calls bpf_obj_free_fields on the destination slot, and returns 0, with the caller retaining ownership of all buffers.
note: Checked arraymap.c:357-394: error order -EINVAL, -E2BIG, -EEXIST (any BPF_NOEXIST bit), -EINVAL (BPF_F_LOCK without spin lock); percpu branch uses this_cpu_ptr + copy_map_value, others copy_map_value_locked when BPF_F_LOCK; bpf_obj_free_fields in both. Prose correct, kept.

name: bpf_percpu_array_update
prose: Precondition: key points to a readable u32 index and value points to a readable buffer of at least nr_possible_cpus * array->elem_size bytes. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if map_flags > BPF_EXIST, otherwise -E2BIG if the index is >= map->max_entries, otherwise -EEXIST if map_flags == BPF_NOEXIST, and in each of these error cases leaves the map unchanged; otherwise it takes the RCU read lock, copies value into every possible CPU's percpu slot for the index (advancing by array->elem_size per CPU), calls bpf_obj_free_fields on each destination slot, releases the RCU read lock, and returns 0, with the caller retaining ownership of all buffers.
note: Checked arraymap.c:396-433: -EINVAL, -E2BIG, -EEXIST (map_flags == BPF_NOEXIST) before rcu_read_lock; loop over possible CPUs with copy_map_value_long and bpf_obj_free_fields; returns 0. Prose correct, kept.

name: __bpf_lru_list_rotate_inactive
prose: Precondition: lru and l are valid, the caller holds the lock protecting l's lists, l->next_inactive_rotation points at a node in l's inactive list or at the inactive list head, and the list linkage is consistent. Postcondition: if the inactive list is empty the function returns immediately with l->next_inactive_rotation unchanged; otherwise it starts at l->next_inactive_rotation (or at the tail if that pointer is the inactive list head), scans toward the list head via prev, wrapping to the tail after the head, examines at most lru->nr_scans nodes and stops after a full cycle, moves every examined node whose ref bit is set to the head of the active list with its ref bit cleared while leaving unreferenced nodes in the inactive list, and sets l->next_inactive_rotation to the list pointer that preceded (toward the list head) the last examined node before any move, or to the inactive list head if no node was examined; it returns void and reports no error.
note: Checked bpf_lru_list.c:152-185 and __bpf_lru_node_move (86-108). Reviewer claims (cursor set to prev of last visited; traversal toward list head via prev) are RIGHT and already in prose (line 175, 184). Detail: cursor is the 'next' captured before the move; head is skipped without counting a scan (169-172). Prose kept.

name: btf_show_name
prose: Requires show to point to an initialized struct btf_show whose btf and state (type_id or member) are valid and whose state.name is a writable buffer of sizeof(show->state.name) bytes. Ensures show->state.name is NUL-terminated and truncated to its size by snprintf (holding the rendered type name with a struct/union/enum prefix that is omitted when a typedef was crossed, member prefix, pointer/array suffixes and parens, or only the parens when BTF_SHOW_NONAME is set) and returns a pointer to that buffer, except that when the type is an array member, the type id cannot be resolved, or the typedef/pointer/array nesting reaches BTF_SHOW_MAX_ITER it leaves show->state.name as the empty string and returns the empty string literal "".
note: Read btf.c:965-1122. Return paths: array_member (990-991), unresolvable id (1007-1009), MAX_ITER reached (1068-1069), and the normal snprintf path (1102-1121). Prose otherwise correct; added snprintf truncation and typedef prefix suppression (1095-1096).

name: __cgroup_bpf_attach
prose: Precondition: cgroup_mutex is held and prog or link is non-null (link must be non-null when prog is null, because link->link.prog is dereferenced). Postcondition: on success it returns 0 after inserting the program or link into cgrp's program list for the resolved attach type (replacing the matched existing entry when BPF_F_REPLACE is set), setting cgrp->bpf.flags[atype] to the new saved flags (only the BPF_F_ALLOW_OVERRIDE / BPF_F_ALLOW_MULTI bits), for BPF_LSM_CGROUP linking a trampoline shim and unlinking the old one on replace, incrementing the static key only when a new entry (not a replacement) was added, incrementing the revision, propagating effective programs to descendants, linking the new cgroup storages, releasing the cgroup's reference to the replaced old program if any, and consuming the caller's reference to prog (when prog is non-null) and to link (when link is non-null) while leaving the caller's replace_prog reference untouched; on failure it returns -EINVAL (invalid flag combination, link/prog conflict, replace_prog/BPF_F_REPLACE mismatch, or unresolvable attach type), -ESTALE (non-zero revision not matching cgrp->bpf.revisions), -EPERM (hierarchy disallows attach or flags mismatch the existing entry), -E2BIG (program list full), -ENOENT or another error from find_attach_entry or insert_pl_to_hlist, -ENOMEM (storage or list allocation failure), or an error from bpf_trampoline_link_cgroup_shim or update_effective_progs, and in every failure case cgrp->bpf.flags is restored, any newly inserted list entry is removed and freed, an existing entry's program, flags and storages are restored, the new storages are freed, and no reference to prog, replace_prog or link is consumed.
note: Read cgroup.c:643-679 (find_attach_entry), 703-789 (get_prog_list, insert_pl_to_hlist) and 806-933. Reviewer round-1 claim (omits -ENOENT from find_attach_entry) is RIGHT but already in the prose (find_attach_entry returns -ENOENT at line 675 and -EINVAL at 661/664; get_prog_list also returns -ENOENT at 762). Round-2 claim (link reference is consumed on success) is RIGHT and already stated ('consuming the caller reference to link'). Added the LSM shim and static-key behaviour (894-911).

name: ___bpf_prog_run
prose: The eBPF interpreter (core.c:1793-2339) runs the program starting at insn with the register file regs (R1 holds the context) and returns when it executes the exit instruction. Dispatch is by computed goto through jumptable[insn->code]. The call instructions (JMP_CALL, JMP_CALL_ARGS) store the result of calling the helper function at __bpf_call_base + imm (or __bpf_call_base_args + imm) with R1..R5 into R0 and continue. JMP_TAIL_CALL treats R2 as a bpf_array map and R3 as the index: if the index is >= max_entries, tail_call_cnt has reached MAX_TAIL_CALL_CNT, or the slot array->ptrs[index] is NULL, the tail call is skipped and execution continues with the next instruction; otherwise tail_call_cnt is incremented and execution jumps to the first instruction of the target program. JMP_EXIT returns the current value of R0. Any opcode that reaches default_label (including unsupported atomic operations) prints a warning "BPF interpreter: unknown opcode", executes BUG_ON(1), and only if that returns would return 0. The function relies on the verifier having validated the program; it performs no checks of its own on jump targets or memory accesses, and acquires no locks.
note: Packet item was an unnamed slice of the interpreter loop; real function is ___bpf_prog_run (core.c:1793). Read 2078-2131 and 2325-2339 and the head at 1785-1821. Old prose was too thin (omitted tail-call skip behaviour and CALL stores), not wrong.

name: bpf_prog_array_copy
prose: Precondition: old_array is NULL or a NULL-terminated prog array, exclude_prog and include_prog may each be NULL, and bpf_cookie is meaningful only when include_prog is non-NULL. Postcondition: returns 0 with *new_array set to a newly allocated NULL-terminated array containing every old_array item whose prog is neither exclude_prog nor dummy_bpf_prog, followed by include_prog with bpf_cookie when include_prog is non-NULL, or set to NULL when that array would be empty; returns -EEXIST if include_prog already appears in old_array, -ENOENT if exclude_prog is non-NULL and absent from old_array, and -ENOMEM if allocation fails, leaving *new_array unmodified on all three error paths.
note: Read core.c:2811-2880. Reviewer round-15 claim (empty result allocates an array, not NULL) is WRONG: code sets *new_array = NULL and returns 0 when new_prog_cnt == 0 (2848-2851). The -EEXIST check is skipped for an entry equal to exclude_prog (continue at 2828-2831); noted in prose is not needed otherwise. Prose kept.

name: cpu_map_generic_redirect
prose: Precondition: rcpu is a valid bpf_cpu_map_entry whose queue ptr_ring and kthread are initialized, and skb is a valid sk_buff with at least skb->mac_len bytes of data at its current data pointer. Postcondition: the function pulls skb->mac_len bytes off the head of skb, calls skb_set_redirected(skb, false), which sets skb->redirected to 1 (and, when CONFIG_NET_REDIRECT is set, from_ingress to false; it does not touch is_atomic), and sets bit 0 of the local skb pointer variable via __ptr_set_bit(0, &skb), so the pointer enqueued has bit 0 set; it then tries to enqueue skb into rcpu->queue with ptr_ring_produce: on success it returns 0, the skb has been handed to the queue so the caller loses ownership of it, and rcpu->kthread is woken with wake_up_process; on failure it returns the negative error code produced by ptr_ring_produce, the skb is not queued so the caller retains ownership of it, and rcpu->kthread is not woken; in both cases trace_xdp_cpumap_enqueue fires with (rcpu->map_id, !ret, !!ret, rcpu->cpu).
note: Read cpumap.c:795-812 and skb_set_redirected (skbuff.h:5310-5318). Reviewer claims rounds 1, 2, 15 all RIGHT: skb_set_redirected sets redirected=1 and from_ingress, not is_atomic; prose corrected.

name: print_bpf_insn
prose: Prints one BPF instruction as text through cbs->cb_print(cbs->private_data, ...), with insn read and, for a BPF_LD | BPF_IMM | BPF_DW instruction, also insn + 1 (disasm.c:186-393). It dispatches on the instruction class. ALU/ALU64 forms print END/bswap, NEG, addr_space_cast, percpu address move, register or immediate operations. STX prints plain stores, the atomic forms ADD/AND/OR/XOR (with or without FETCH), CMPXCHG, XCHG, LOAD_ACQ and STORE_REL, and otherwise a "BUG_%02x" line. ST prints an immediate store, "nospec" for mode 0xc0, or "BUG_st_%02x". LDX prints a load for modes BPF_MEM or BPF_MEMSX, otherwise "BUG_ldx_%02x" and returns. LD prints ABS and IND packet loads, the 64-bit immediate load (immediate forced to 0 when the source register is one of BPF_PSEUDO_MAP_FD, MAP_VALUE, MAP_IDX, MAP_IDX_VALUE or BTF_ID and allow_ptr_leaks is false; the text comes from cbs->cb_imm if set, else "0x%llx"), or otherwise "BUG_ld_%02x" and returns. JMP/JMP32 prints call (for BPF_PSEUDO_CALL as "pc" plus the name from __func_get_name, else the helper name from __func_get_name, whose buffer starts as "unknown" and is replaced by a helper id name, by cbs->cb_call, or by "kernel-function" for a kfunc call), goto, may_goto, gotol, exit and the conditional jumps. Any other class prints the class name. It returns void and acquires no locks or references.
note: Packet slice cut the head; real function print_bpf_insn at disasm.c:186-393 read in full (and __func_get_name 16-41). Reviewer round-15 claim ('unknown' is only the initial buffer value, overwritten by __func_get_name) is RIGHT (355-359, 22-40); old prose said 'printing unknown for non-PSEUDO_CALL calls', now corrected. Also added the missing BUG_st_%02x and the other atomic forms.

name: bpf_get_current_pid_tgid
prose: Requires nothing; the helper may be called from any context. Returns the u64 two's-complement encoding of -EINVAL (18446744073709551594) when there is no current task, and otherwise returns the current task's thread group id in the high 32 bits and its pid in the low 32 bits (so the value is (u64)tgid << 32 | pid, which is 0 for the idle task where both are 0); the caller gains no locks, references or memory.
note: Read helpers.c:224-232: -EINVAL when current is NULL; else (u64)task->tgid << 32 | task->pid. Prose correct, kept.

name: bpf_dynptr_check_size
prose: Precondition: size is any u32 value. Postcondition: the function returns -7 (the errno value E2BIG) when size is greater than 16777215 (2^24 - 1, DYNPTR_MAX_SIZE), and returns 0 otherwise; it takes no locks and acquires or releases no references or memory.
note: Read helpers.c:1717-1720 and the definition DYNPTR_MAX_SIZE = (1UL << 24) - 1 at line 1680; prose correct. The old contract was rejected only by a mechanical complaint about naming E2BIG; rewritten as a plain two-case contract using -7.

name: bpf_task_work_irq
prose: Precondition: irq_work points to the irq_work field of a valid struct bpf_task_work_ctx whose task, mode, and state fields are initialized and which owns one reference consumed by this irq_work invocation. Postcondition: the function runs under an RCU tasks-trace read-side section that it acquires and releases, and returns after either releasing the invocation's ctx reference without changing state when the state was not BPF_TW_PENDING, or, when task_work_add fails, resetting ctx->prog and ctx->task, attempting to restore BPF_TW_STANDBY (leaving BPF_TW_FREED if it has already been set), and releasing the invocation's ctx reference, or, when task_work_add succeeds, attempting to move the state from BPF_TW_SCHEDULING to BPF_TW_SCHEDULED and, if the state is BPF_TW_FREED, cancelling the task work (releasing one ctx reference if cancellation succeeds, otherwise leaving that reference to the scheduled callback).
note: Read helpers.c:4048-4083. Prose matches: non-PENDING early return with ctx put (4056-4058); task_work_add failure path (4061-4070); success cmpxchg SCHEDULING->SCHEDULED and cancel on FREED (4080-4082). Reviewer round-1 claim (omits non-PENDING bailout and FREED cancel) now covered; round-2 claim (precondition wrongly requires caller-held rcu tasks-trace) is RIGHT that the function takes its own guard (4054), and the precondition does not require it. Prose kept.

name: bpf_bprintf_prepare
prose: Precondition: fmt points to at least fmt_size readable bytes and contains a NUL byte within them, raw_args points to at least num_args readable u64 values, and data is a valid struct bpf_bprintf_data whose bin_args and buf fields are NULL when the corresponding get_bin_args/get_buf flag is false. Postcondition: the function returns -EINVAL if no NUL is found within fmt_size bytes, if fmt contains an ASCII byte that is neither printable nor isspace() (so tab, newline, vertical tab, form feed and carriage return are accepted), if a byte after '%' is non-ASCII, if a conversion specifier is unsupported, or if a specifier appears when num_spec has already reached num_args; -EBUSY if buffers are requested and the per-CPU bprintf nest level is already MAX_BPRINTF_NEST_LEVEL; -ENOSPC if a %s or %c conversion finds the binary argument buffer exactly full, if a %p[Ii][46] conversion has fewer than 4 or 16 bytes left, or if a numeric conversion has fewer than its argument size left; and 0 otherwise, in which case if buffers were requested ((data->get_bin_args && num_args != 0) || data->get_buf) per-CPU buffers are held with preemption disabled, data->buf points into them when get_buf is true, data->bin_args points into them when get_bin_args is true and num_args != 0 (and is NULL otherwise), and the caller must call bpf_bprintf_cleanup to release them, while if no buffers were requested no buffers are held, preemption is not disabled, data->bin_args is set to NULL when get_bin_args is true (and left untouched otherwise), data->buf is left untouched, and bpf_bprintf_cleanup is a no-op; on any error return any buffers acquired are released before returning without clearing the data pointers.
note: Read helpers.c:817-1061. Reviewer round-15 claim (code also permits tab/newline and other isspace bytes) is RIGHT (line 853) and prose corrected. Round-2 claim (-ENOSPC swallowed for %s) is WRONG: -ENOSPC is returned only when tmp_buf_end == tmp_buf (984-987); a bpf_trace_copy_string failure is converted to an empty string with err = 1 (993-996). Round-1 claim (verification-only mode with no buffers) is RIGHT and already in the prose (no buffers case).

name: do_call_rcu_ttrace
prose: Precondition: c is a per-cpu bpf_mem_cache whose free_by_rcu_ttrace and waiting_for_gp_ttrace lists are only manipulated by the cpu executing this call (irq_work or RCU-callback context, as when invoked from free_bulk or from __free_by_rcu), and c->call_rcu_ttrace_in_progress is the flag guarding re-entry. Postcondition: the function returns void; if the in-progress flag was 0, every node on free_by_rcu_ttrace is moved to waiting_for_gp_ttrace and then either, when c->draining is set, __free_rcu is called synchronously so those nodes are freed immediately (c->dtor, if set, is invoked on every node, and the node memory is freed, plus the per-CPU area for per-CPU caches) and the flag is reset to 0 before return, or call_rcu_tasks_trace is scheduled so __free_rcu_tasks_trace/__free_rcu later frees those nodes and resets the flag to 0; if the flag was already 1, then when c->draining is set the nodes on free_by_rcu_ttrace are freed immediately under c->lock and the flag is left at 1, otherwise the lists are left unchanged and nothing is scheduled; a WARN_ON_ONCE fires (without changing state) if waiting_for_gp_ttrace was non-empty on entry with flag 0.
note: Read memalloc.c:257-340. Reviewer round-15 claim (free_all invokes c->dtor on every node, not only non-percpu nodes) is RIGHT (271-273); prose corrected. Round-1 claim (called from RCU callback too) is RIGHT and already covered in the precondition.

name: load_skel
prose: Precondition: the function is called at most once, before the static skel, maps_link and progs_link globals are otherwise used, since it overwrites skel without freeing any previously opened skeleton. Postcondition: it returns 0 on success, with the iterators skeleton opened, loaded and attached, maps_link and progs_link holding new references stored in the static globals, and the skeleton's dump_bpf_map_fd and dump_bpf_prog_fd closed and zeroed; otherwise it returns a negative errno - -ENOMEM when iterators_bpf__open returned NULL, in which case skel is NULL and no cleanup runs, or the error from iterators_bpf__load, iterators_bpf__attach or the PTR_ERR of a failed bpf_link_get_from_fd, in which case free_links_and_skel() has destroyed the skeleton and put any valid references held in maps_link and progs_link, while the static pointers skel, maps_link and progs_link are not reset: after a failed bpf_link_get_from_fd the corresponding link pointer holds an ERR_PTR, and after the cleanup a successfully obtained link pointer still holds the address whose reference was just put.
note: Read bpf_preload_kern.c:38-72. Reviewer claims: round-2 (free_links_and_skel not run on -ENOMEM) RIGHT and already corrected in prose; round-15 (statics overwritten with ERR_PTR on get_from_fd failure, not unchanged) RIGHT (51-60), prose corrected. Old contract dropped: the function mutates static globals (rule 4).

name: bpf_fd_reuseport_array_update_elem
prose: Updates slot *key of a reuseport sockarray from a socket file descriptor (reuseport_array.c:232-313). It returns -EINVAL if map_flags > BPF_EXIST, -E2BIG if the index is >= map->max_entries, and -EINVAL if the value is a 64-bit fd above S32_MAX (when value_size is 8; otherwise it reads a 32-bit fd). It calls sockfd_lookup (returning its error on failure); from here the socket reference is dropped with sockfd_put on every return. It returns -EINVAL if the socket has no sk. It runs reuseport_array_update_check once without locks (using unlocked reads of the slot and sk_reuseport_cb) and, if that returns an error, returns it: -EEXIST (existing sk and BPF_NOEXIST), -ENOENT (no sk and BPF_EXIST), -ENOTSUPP for a protocol that is not UDP/TCP, a family that is not AF_INET/AF_INET6, or a type that is not SOCK_STREAM/SOCK_DGRAM, -EINVAL if the sk lacks SOCK_RCU_FREE, is not hashed or has no reuseport group, or -EBUSY if sk_user_data is already set. It then takes spin_lock_bh(&reuseport_lock) and the new sk's sk_callback_lock for writing, repeats the check with locked reads, and on error returns it (after releasing both locks). On success it sets nsk->sk_user_data to the slot address tagged with SK_USER_DATA_NOCOPY | SK_USER_DATA_BPF, publishes nsk in array->ptrs[index] with rcu_assign_pointer, releases the new sk lock, then clears the replaced socket's sk_user_data under its sk_callback_lock (if there was one), releases reuseport_lock, drops the socket reference and returns 0. Locks are released on every return; array->ptrs[index] is unchanged on every error return.
note: Packet slice began mid-function; real name bpf_fd_reuseport_array_update_elem (reuseport_array.c:232). Read 187-313. Old prose lacked -ENOTSUPP/-EBUSY and the double-check structure but was otherwise consistent.

name: __sys_bpf
prose: Precondition: cmd is a BPF command number, uattr is a bpfptr_t describing the attribute buffer (user or kernel memory) and size is the attribute length the caller claims; the caller may sleep. Postcondition: the function returns the negative error from bpf_check_uarg_tail_zero if the bytes of the attribute beyond size are non-zero (-E2BIG) or cannot be read (-EFAULT); it then clamps size to sizeof(union bpf_attr), zeroes a local attr, copies that many bytes from uattr and returns -EFAULT if the copy fails; it returns the negative error from security_bpf if that hook fails; otherwise it returns the value produced by the handler selected by cmd (0, a non-negative value such as a file descriptor or id, or a negative errno), or -EINVAL if cmd is not a supported BPF command; no locks, references or memory are retained on return.
note: Read syscall.c:6163-6307. Reviewer claims: round-1 (size clamp is done by function; early -EFAULT/security returns) RIGHT and in prose; round-2 (bpf_check_uarg_tail_zero returns -E2BIG) RIGHT and already stated; round-15 (handlers such as BPF_MAP_CREATE/PROG_LOAD/OBJ_GET return non-negative fds) RIGHT, prose corrected. The default case returns -EINVAL (6302).

name: bpf_unpriv_handler
prose: Precondition: table and table->data point to valid storage with table->data pointing to a writable int, and buffer, lenp and ppos are valid for proc_dointvec_minmax. Postcondition: if write is zero, it returns proc_dointvec_minmax's return value without modifying *table->data or calling unpriv_ebpf_notify; if write is nonzero and the caller lacks CAP_SYS_ADMIN, it returns -EPERM without side effects; otherwise it calls proc_dointvec_minmax with a copy of table whose data points to a local int initialized from *table->data, and then: if that call returns 0 and the original value was 1 and the parsed value is not 1, it returns -EPERM without updating *table->data and without calling unpriv_ebpf_notify; if that call returns 0 in all other cases, it stores the parsed value into *table->data; and in the write case, except for the two -EPERM returns above, it calls unpriv_ebpf_notify with the local value (also when proc_dointvec_minmax failed, in which case the local value is still the old one) and returns proc_dointvec_minmax's return value.
note: Read syscall.c:6520-6542. Reviewer round-1 claim (no notify on locked-state -EPERM) RIGHT (6533-6534 returns before 6538); round-15 claim (write==0 and missing CAP_SYS_ADMIN skip notify) RIGHT: those are the first two branches of the prose already; the final clause is now explicit about the write case.

name: check_helper_call
prose: Verifier check for a BPF helper call instruction insn (verifier.c:11680-12248); *insn_idx_p is the instruction index. It resolves the helper prototype with get_helper_proto (-EINVAL for -ERANGE, otherwise that error), then rejects with -EINVAL a GPL-only helper in a non-GPL program, a helper whose allowed() callback refuses the program, a sleeping helper in a non-sleepable program, and a sleeping helper called under an RCU, preempt-disabled or IRQ-disabled section; it returns -EFAULT (verifier bug) if a packet-data-changing helper does not take ctx in R1, and the error from check_func_proto if the prototype is malformed. It then runs check_func_arg for each of the argument registers, record_func_map, record_func_key and check_mem_access for any meta.access_size bytes, returning the first error. It releases the reference or dynptr named by meta.release_regno (errors returned; -EFAULT for releasing a CONST_PTR_TO_DYNPTR). A per-helper switch performs extra checks: tail_call leak check, get_local_storage (-EINVAL unless R2 is NULL), callback-pushing helpers via push_callback_call, snprintf, loop, dynptr_from_mem (-EACCES unless R1 is PTR_TO_MAP_VALUE), set_retval, dynptr_data and dynptr_write (several -EFAULT verifier-bug checks), per_cpu_ptr/this_cpu_ptr and user_ringbuf_drain, and returns on any error. It marks the caller-saved registers not initialised and sets R0 from the helper return type (unknown scalar, not-init for void, or a pointer with map, BTF, mem_size, ref_obj_id and dynptr_id metadata, with a fresh id when it may be NULL); an invalid or unknown return type returns -EINVAL or -EFAULT. It then may call acquire_reference (negative result returned), do_refine_retval_range and check_map_func_compatibility (errors returned), obtains callchain buffers for get_stack/get_task_stack (the error from get_callchain_buffers is returned; -ENOTSUPP only when CONFIG_PERF_EVENTS is off), returns -ENOTSUPP when check_get_func_ip fails, and for tail_call inside a callback returns -EINVAL, otherwise handles the frame exit. On success it returns 0 after clearing packet pointers if the helper changes packet data. The verifier state may already have been modified when an error is returned.
note: Slice cut the head; real function check_helper_call at verifier.c:11680-12248 read with returns/gotos listed. Reviewer round-15 claim (-ENOTSUPP only for missing CONFIG_PERF_EVENTS; get_callchain_buffers failure returns its own error) is RIGHT (12192-12200); prose corrected. -ENOTSUPP is also returned at 12211. I did not enumerate every -EINVAL/-EFAULT site.

name: check_kfunc_args
prose: Validates every argument of a kfunc call described by meta (verifier.c:13395-13939); the packet slice was the middle of this function's per-argument loop, not a function of its own. It returns -EINVAL if the function prototype has more than MAX_BPF_FUNC_REG_ARGS arguments. For each argument i (register R(i+1)) it skips ignored arguments; records a prog->aux argument (-EFAULT if more than one); for scalar BTF types requires a SCALAR_VALUE register (-EINVAL), handles constant arguments (-EINVAL if not a known constant, mark_chain_precision error, -EFAULT if two) and rdonly_buf_size/rdwr_buf_size arguments (-EINVAL for a second one, a non-constant, or a value above U32_MAX) and continues. For pointer arguments it classifies the argument with get_kfunc_ptr_arg_type (its negative result is returned), returns -EINVAL or -EACCES for NULL, type, trusted, RCU, refcounted or map-uid mismatches, records metadata in meta for release arguments and map pointers, and dispatches by kind to handlers (process_dynptr_func, process_iter_arg, process_kf_arg_ptr_to_list_head / rbtree_root / list_node / rbtree_node / btf_id, check_mem_reg, check_kfunc_mem_size_reg, check_reg_const_str, process_wq_func, process_task_work_func, process_irq_flag, process_spin_lock), returning the first error from them. After the loop it returns -EINVAL if the kfunc is a release function but no release register was found, and otherwise 0. meta and the verifier state may have been partly updated when an error is returned. It takes no locks.
note: Name was 'process_kf_arg' in the packet but that name is not defined; the slice (verifier.c:13473-13768) lies inside check_kfunc_args (13395-13939). Read all return/goto sites; prose is a per-class summary, not a per-case listing; the old prose described one argument, not the loop.

name: regs_refine_cond_op
prose: Precondition: reg1 and reg2 point to valid, initialized bpf_reg_state objects whose min/max bounds and var_off tnums describe the states on the branch path, opcode is a BPF jump opcode (possibly BPF_JSET|BPF_X), and is_jmp32 selects the 32-bit or 64-bit view. Postcondition: for JGE/JGT/JSGE/JSGT the opcode is first flipped and the two register pointers swapped; for JEQ both registers' min/max bounds are intersected and their tnums intersected (subreg tnums for 32-bit); for JNE, if reg2 (after a possible swap) is a constant, reg1's bounds are moved one step off that constant when they equal it; for JSET, if reg2 (after a possible swap) is a constant power of two, reg1's tnum is OR-ed with that constant; for JSET|BPF_X, if reg2 (after a possible swap) is a constant, reg1's bounds are reset to unbounded and its tnum is AND-ed with the complement of that constant; for JLE/JLT/JSLE/JSLT the unsigned or signed bounds of both registers are narrowed; for unhandled opcodes the function returns without changing anything, and for JNE, JSET and JSET|BPF_X nothing is changed when neither register is a constant (even after the swap); JEQ and JLE/JLT/JSLE/JSLT narrow bounds without needing a constant; the caller retains ownership of both registers.
note: Read verifier.c:16731-16899. Reviewer round-15 claim (JEQ and JLE/JLT/JSLE/JSLT narrow without a constant, so the 'no constant operand' clause is wrong) is RIGHT: only JNE/JSET/JSET|X require a constant (16780-16783, 16819-16822, 16844-16847). Prose corrected.

name: check_return_code
prose: Checks the value in register regno at program exit (verifier.c:17711-17908), in the context of frame 0 of the current verifier state; reg_name is used only for messages. Early returns 0 before the register is examined, only when frame 0 is the main program or an exception callback: an LSM program that is not BPF_LSM_CGROUP and whose attach function prototype has a void return, a struct_ops program whose attach prototype has a void return, and (for a struct_ops main program) __check_ptr_off_reg's result when the register's BTF type equals the resolved return pointer type and has a ref_obj_id. Otherwise it calls check_reg_arg (error returned) and returns -EACCES if the register holds a pointer. For an async callback it uses the callback's return range and goes to enforcement. For a non-exception subprogram exit it returns -EINVAL if the register is not scalar, else 0. Otherwise it picks a range by program type: CGROUP_SOCK_ADDR recvmsg/getpeername/getsockname types 1..1 and bind types 0..3, CGROUP_SKB egress 0..3 (also marking enforce_expected_attach_type when the register tnum lies within 2..3), RAW_TRACEPOINT 0..0 (returns 0 if no attach_btf_id), TRACING fentry/fexit 0..0, iter default 0..1, raw_tp and modify_return return 0, any other tracing attach type returns -ENOTSUPP, KPROBE session types 0..1 and other kprobe types return 0, SK_LOOKUP SK_DROP..SK_PASS, NETFILTER NF_DROP..NF_ACCEPT, LSM non-cgroup uses the hook's return range (returns 0 if none or the full s32 range, and checks 32-bit) while BPF_LSM_CGROUP on a void hook uses 1..1, struct_ops with a return type 0..0 (0 returned if none), and EXT and all other types return 0; the default range is 0..1. At enforcement it returns -EINVAL if the register is not a scalar, the error from mark_chain_precision, -EINVAL if the register is outside the range, else 0. No locks are taken.
note: Read verifier.c:17711-17908. Reviewer claims all RIGHT: void LSM/struct_ops return 0 before readability checks (17726-17737); BPF_LSM_CGROUP on a void hook enforces range 1..1 (17859-17864) rather than returning 0; non-exception subprogram non-scalar exit returns -EINVAL (17779-17784). Old prose was garbled; rewritten from the code.

name: __mark_chain_precision
prose: Back-propagates precision marks from starting_state for register regno (or, with regno < 0, for the backtrack state already set in env->bt) (verifier.c:4820-5003). It returns 0 immediately if env->bpf_capable is false. It initialises env->bt for the starting frame; if regno >= 0 and that register is not a SCALAR_VALUE it reports a verifier bug and returns -EFAULT, else it marks the register in the backtrack set. If the backtrack set is empty it returns 0. It then walks instructions backwards through each state and its parent chain, calling backtrack_insn for every instruction except the first: -ENOTSUPP calls mark_all_scalars_precise(starting_state) and returns 0 (this marks scalar registers and spilled scalar stack slots in the parent states, not in starting_state itself) while any other error is returned; the walk returns 0 as soon as the backtrack set becomes empty; it returns -EFAULT (verifier bug) if the previous instruction index is >= prog->len, if the function-entry state is reached with a non-argument register or stack mask pending, or if a stack-slot index is beyond the parent's allocated stack. When the function-entry state is reached with only argument registers pending, scalar argument registers of frame 0 are marked precise and 0 is returned. In each parent state it sets precise on scalar registers and spilled scalar stack slots named in the backtrack set; *changed (a local if changed is NULL) is set to true when a precise flag is newly set in those paths. If the walk ends at the root with registers still pending it calls mark_all_scalars_precise and resets the backtrack state, then returns 0. It takes no locks.
note: Read verifier.c:4661-4700 and 4820-5003. Reviewer claims: round-1 (-ENOTSUPP returns 0 after mark_all_scalars_precise) RIGHT; round-2 (starting state not marked, including the fallback) RIGHT (4679 loops from st->parent); round-15 (the visible -EFAULT checks the instruction index >= prog->len, not a stack slot) is PARTLY WRONG: both exist: stack slot check at 4956-4959 and instruction index at 4922-4930; the prose now lists all three -EFAULT sites. Note mark_all_scalars_precise does not set *changed (not passed).

name: check_stack_read_fixed_off
prose: Handles a read of size bytes at constant negative stack offset off from stack function state reg_state (verifier.c:5479-5605); reg_state is the frame the stack pointer points to (the caller passes func(env, reg)), which can differ from the current frame env->cur_state->frame[curframe]. dst_regno is the destination register in the current frame, or negative when no register receives the data. It scratches the slot, runs check_fastcall_stack_contract, and calls bpf_mark_stack_read (its error is returned). If the slot is a spilled register: for a read that is not a full BPF_REG_SIZE read of a full BPF_REG_SIZE spill, a non-scalar spilled register gives -EACCES; with dst_regno < 0 it returns 0 immediately; otherwise a narrowing fill copies the spilled scalar state (keeping the destination subreg_def, clearing the scalar id if the spill is wider than the read) and any other partial read is validated byte by byte (STACK_SPILL, STACK_MISC, STACK_ZERO, or STACK_INVALID when allow_uninit_stack, else -EACCES) and then sets the destination to constant zero or an unknown scalar; a full-size spill read copies the spilled register state into dst_regno when dst_regno >= 0, or returns -EACCES if dst_regno < 0 and the spilled value is a pointer that would leak (not allow_ptr_leaks). If the slot is not a spill, each byte must be STACK_MISC, STACK_ZERO or STACK_INVALID with allow_uninit_stack (else -EACCES) and the destination, if any, is set by mark_reg_stack_read. In the paths that reach the end, if the instruction-history flags are non-zero it returns the result of push_jmp_history (0 or a negative errno), otherwise 0.
note: Read verifier.c:5479-5605. Reviewer claims all RIGHT: STACK_INVALID is allowed with allow_uninit_stack, STACK_SPILL is allowed in the mixed-read loop, and reg_state is the frame of the pointed-to stack (from the caller's func(env, reg), see check_stack_read 5673) not necessarily the current frame; the negative-offset slot arithmetic (-off - 1) is why the old contract was wrong.

name: update_parent_effective_cpumask
prose: Applies a partition command cmd (partcmd_enable, partcmd_enablei, partcmd_disable, partcmd_update or partcmd_invalidate) for cpuset cs against its parent's effective CPUs (cpuset.c:1829-2158). The caller must hold cpuset_mutex (lockdep assertion) and cs must not be a remote partition (WARN_ON_ONCE). Returns 0 with no change for partcmd_invalidate when cs is already an invalid partition. Otherwise, direct returns that do not write cs->prs_err are: PERR_INVPARENT (parent in an invalid partition state) or PERR_NOTPART (parent not a valid partition); PERR_CPUSEMPTY when newmask is NULL and cs's xcpus are empty; for enable/enablei, PERR_INVCPUS (computed exclusive CPUs empty), PERR_HKEEPING (housekeeping conflict, or isolated CPUs cannot be updated) and PERR_NOCPUS (tasks would be left without a CPU). For disable it marks the partition a member and returns CPUs to the parent. For update, with or without newmask, error conditions (empty newmask: PERR_CPUSEMPTY; PERR_HKEEPING; PERR_NOCPUS; PERR_NOTEXCL when an invalid partition's CPUs are not exclusive with its siblings) are stored in cs->prs_err and flip a valid root/isolated partition to its invalid state (or an invalid one to valid when no error) but are not themselves returned. For invalidate, the partition becomes invalid and the CPUs are returned. If nothing is to be added or deleted and the state is unchanged it returns 0. For non-update commands whose state changes it returns update_partition_exclusive_flag's error if non-zero. Otherwise, under callback_lock (spin_lock_irq), it updates cs->partition_root_state and nr_subparts, moves CPUs between the parent's effective masks (partition_xcpus_del / partition_xcpus_add) and adjusts the parent's nr_subparts; after the lock it updates isolation cpumasks, for update commands calls update_partition_exclusive_flag (result ignored), updates the parent's tasks and sibling cpumasks when CPUs were added or deleted, rebalances scheduler domains for update without newmask, calls notify_partition_change and returns 0. rcu_read_lock is taken only in the update-without-newmask branch, and released there.
note: Name in the packet was update_parent_subparts_cpumask, which does not exist; real function update_parent_effective_cpumask at cpuset.c:1829-2158 read in full. Old prose was WRONG in saying PERR_NOTEXCL and the non-exclusive invalid-to-valid conversion are direct returns with prs_err untouched: they set part_error, which is stored in cs->prs_err at write_error (2066-2068) while the function returns 0.

name: cpuset_can_attach
prose: Precondition: tset is a valid, non-empty cgroup taskset and the caller does not hold cpuset_mutex; the function records the first task's cpuset in the global cpuset_attach_old_cs. Postcondition: cpuset_mutex is acquired and released; on success (return 0) cs->attach_in_progress has been incremented and, if DL tasks are being migrated and oldcs->effective_cpus and cs->effective_cpus do not intersect, DL bandwidth has been allocated with dl_bw_alloc (to be freed by cpuset_cancel_attach or kept after a successful attach); on failure it returns -ENOSPC when cs->effective_cpus is empty or, outside v2 mode, cs->mems_allowed is empty, the error returned by task_can_attach for some task, the error from security_task_setscheduler (which is called only when not in cpuset v2 mode or when the effective cpus or mems differ), -EINVAL when DL tasks migrate with disjoint old and new effective_cpus but no active CPU of cs->effective_cpus exists, or the error returned by dl_bw_alloc, and in every failure case cs->nr_migrate_dl_tasks and cs->sum_migrate_dl_bw are reset to zero and attach_in_progress is not incremented.
note: Read cpuset.c:3212-3285. Reviewer round-15 claim (omits the dl_bw_alloc error) is RIGHT (3268-3270). Also noted the conditional security hook (3245). cpuset_attach_old_cs is written before the mutex is taken (3221), as the precondition already says.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE3(sigprocmask, int, how,
prose: Generated function compat_sys_sigprocmask(how, nset, oset). Precondition: nset, when non-NULL, points to readable user memory holding a compat_old_sigset_t, and oset, when non-NULL, points to writable user memory for a compat_old_sigset_t. Postcondition: it returns -EFAULT without changing the blocked set if reading *nset fails (nset non-NULL), returns -EINVAL without changing the blocked set if nset is non-NULL and how is not SIG_BLOCK, SIG_UNBLOCK or SIG_SETMASK, and otherwise, when nset is non-NULL, replaces the current task's blocked set by the old set with the supplied mask added, removed or substituted per how (SIGKILL and SIGSTOP bits cleared from the supplied mask); it then stores the first word of the blocked set as it was before any update into *oset if oset is non-NULL, returning -EFAULT if that store fails (in which case the blocked set has already been updated), and returns 0 otherwise.
note: Read compat.c:40-77: old_set captured at 47 before any update; get_user failure -EFAULT (50-51); SIGKILL/SIGSTOP masked out; invalid how returns -EINVAL before set_current_blocked; put_user failure returns -EFAULT after the update. Prose correct, kept.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE3(sched_setaffinity, compat_pid_t, pid,
prose: Generated function compat_sys_sched_setaffinity(pid, len, user_mask_ptr). Precondition: user_mask_ptr points to readable user memory of at least min(len, cpumask_size()) bytes. Postcondition: it returns -ENOMEM if the temporary cpumask cannot be allocated; otherwise it builds the mask by zeroing it first when len < cpumask_size() and then reading min(len, cpumask_size()) bytes of bitmap from user_mask_ptr, returning -EFAULT if that user copy fails, and otherwise returns the value returned by sched_setaffinity(pid, new_mask); the temporary cpumask, once allocated, is freed before returning.
note: Read compat.c:110-142: compat_get_user_cpu_mask zero-fills when len < cpumask_size and truncates len to cpumask_size; alloc failure -ENOMEM; read failure returns its error to the caller (an -EFAULT-class error); mask freed at 140. Prose correct, kept.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE3(sched_getaffinity, compat_pid_t,  pid, unsigned int, len,
prose: Generated function compat_sys_sched_getaffinity(pid, len, user_mask_ptr). Precondition: user_mask_ptr points to writable user memory of at least min(len, cpumask_size()) bytes (used only on the success path). Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if len * BITS_PER_BYTE is less than nr_cpu_ids or if len is not a multiple of sizeof(compat_ulong_t), and -ENOMEM if the temporary cpumask cannot be allocated; otherwise it calls sched_getaffinity(pid, mask) and returns its nonzero result unchanged without writing to user memory, or, when that call returns 0, writes min(len, cpumask_size()) bytes of the mask to user_mask_ptr and returns that byte count, or returns -EFAULT if that user copy fails; the temporary cpumask, once allocated, is freed before returning.
note: Read compat.c:144-170: -EINVAL for len*8 < nr_cpu_ids or len not a multiple of sizeof(compat_ulong_t); -ENOMEM; nonzero sched_getaffinity result returned unchanged; success returns retlen = min(len, cpumask_size()) or -EFAULT; mask freed before return. Prose correct, kept.

name: cpuhp_smt_disable
prose: Precondition: ctrlval is one of CPU_SMT_ENABLED, CPU_SMT_DISABLED, or CPU_SMT_FORCE_DISABLED. Postcondition: the function holds the cpu maps lock for its duration; it attempts to offline each online CPU that is not a primary thread, except that when ctrlval is CPU_SMT_ENABLED it skips CPUs for which cpu_smt_thread_allowed(cpu) is true; for each CPU it offlines via cpu_down_maps_locked(cpu, CPUHP_OFFLINE) and on success marks the CPU's device offline and sends a KOBJ_OFFLINE uevent; if any cpu_down_maps_locked call fails it stops immediately, leaves cpu_smt_control unchanged, and returns that negative error code; if all such calls succeed (or there are no such CPUs) it sets cpu_smt_control to ctrlval and returns 0.
note: Read cpu.c:2667-2701 (head, loop, assignment of cpu_smt_control). Prose matches: skips primary threads, skips allowed threads when ctrlval is CPU_SMT_ENABLED, stops on the first cpu_down_maps_locked error and leaves cpu_smt_control unchanged. Reviewer claims about the contract precondition do not apply to the prose.

name: __cpuhp_kick_ap
prose: Precondition: st points to the valid cpuhp_cpu_state of the CPU whose AP hotplug thread is being driven. Postcondition: if st->single is false and st->state already equals st->target, the function returns immediately leaving st->result, st->should_run and the AP thread untouched; otherwise it sets st->result to 0, executes a memory barrier, sets st->should_run to true, wakes st->thread, and blocks until the AP thread has completed the requested work (a single state callback when st->single is true, otherwise the callback range toward st->target), after which st->result holds the AP thread's outcome (0 on success or its error code) and the function returns no value.
note: Read cpu.c:762-776. Early return when !st->single && state == target (764-765); otherwise result reset, smp_mb, should_run, wake_up_process, wait_for_ap_thread. Prose correct, kept; whether the AP thread runs one callback or a range is determined by st->single, as the prose states (round-1 and round-2 claims are covered).

name: reserve_crashkernel_low
prose: Precondition: low_size is any unsigned long long allocation size and the caller owns the crashkernel low reservation state. Postcondition: on a 64-bit build, if memblock_phys_alloc_range(low_size, CRASH_ALIGN, 0, CRASH_ADDR_LOW_MAX) succeeds, the function records the reserved range in crashk_low_res (and inserts it into iomem_resource when HAVE_ARCH_ADD_CRASH_RES_TO_IOMEM_EARLY is defined) and returns 0; if that allocation fails it returns -12 (ENOMEM) without changing crashk_low_res or reserving memory, while on a 32-bit build the body compiles out and the function returns 0 without reserving anything.
note: Read crash_reserve.c:369-390 (compiled only under CONFIG_ARCH_HAS_GENERIC_CRASHKERNEL_RESERVATION, __init). Allocation failure returns -ENOMEM before touching crashk_low_res (374-378); success also logs with pr_info. Contract removed because the function mutates the global crashk_low_res and reserves memblock memory (rule 4).

name: gdb_serial_stub
prose: Runs the kgdb serial (gdb remote protocol) command loop for the stopped CPU in ks (gdbstub.c:955-1091). It clears the output buffer, sets kgdb_usethread to the CPU's task, sets ks->kgdb_usethreadid and clears ks->pass_exception. If kgdb_connected is set it sends a 'T' stop-reply packet (signal and thread id) with put_packet. Then it loops: clears the output buffer, reads a packet with get_packet into remcom_in_buffer, and dispatches on the first character to the gdb_cmd_* handlers (status, registers, memory, binary write, query, task, thread, breakpoints, optionally register get/set), replying with put_packet after each handled packet. Packets 'D' and 'k' call gdb_cmd_detachkill and then go to the default handling; 'R' goes to default handling only if gdb_cmd_reboot returns non-zero; with CONFIG_KGDB_KDB a '3' packet with an empty second character calls gdb_cmd_detachkill and returns DBG_PASS_EVENT immediately; 'C' calls gdb_cmd_exception_pass, which leads to default handling when it returns > 0, to a reply when 0, and to the continue handling when < 0. 'c', 's' and default packets: if kgdb_contthread is set and is not current the loop replies with an -EINVAL error packet and continues; otherwise kgdb_arch_handle_exception is called with the packet, and if its return value is >= 0 or the packet was 'D' or 'k' the loop ends with error = 0 (a negative value keeps the loop running and the output buffer is sent). After the loop it returns 1 if ks->pass_exception was set, otherwise 0; the only other return is DBG_PASS_EVENT for the '3' packet.
note: Read gdbstub.c:955-1091. Reviewer claims: round-1 (can return negative on D/k) is WRONG: error is set to 0 at 1077 before kgdb_exit; round-2 (returns 0 on exit not the arch handler's error) RIGHT; round-15 (the code tests error >= 0 to decide whether to leave the loop, so the return value is not simply discarded) RIGHT (1075-1079): the old 'discarded' wording corrected.

name: kdb_input_flush
prose: Discards pending console input by polling the NULL-terminated array kdb_poll_funcs (kdb_io.c:478-497); it returns void and takes no locks. It starts with flush_delay = 1 and, on each outer pass, decrements it and calls touch_nmi_watchdog. It then calls each poll function in order; as soon as one returns a value other than -1 it sets flush_delay = 1 and restarts the scan from the first function immediately, with no delay. When a full scan finds no input, it calls mdelay(1) only if flush_delay is 1, that is only if some input was seen earlier; the outer loop then runs one more scan (decrementing flush_delay to 0) and returns after a scan that finds no input, otherwise it restarts as above. Hence it returns right after the first scan when no input was pending, and otherwise only after a 1 ms delay followed by a further quiet scan.
note: Read kdb_io.c:478-497. Reviewer claims all RIGHT: round-1 (no quiet period when nothing pending), round-2 (restart is immediate via goto, delay follows a quiet scan), round-15 (mdelay follows a quiet scan once flush_delay is set, not a scan that saw input). The old prose said the opposite for the delay placement; rewritten.

name: kdb_search_string
prose: Precondition: 'searched' and 'searchfor' are null-terminated strings and the globals kdb_grep_leading and kdb_grep_trailing hold the caller's anchoring flags. Postcondition: the function returns 1 if a match is found and 0 otherwise, without modifying memory, locks or references; it returns 0 whenever strlen(searched)-1 is less than strlen(searchfor); with both flags set it returns 1 exactly when strlen(searched)-1 equals strlen(searchfor) and the first strlen(searchfor) bytes of 'searched' equal 'searchfor'; with only kdb_grep_leading set it returns 1 when the first strlen(searchfor) bytes of 'searched' equal 'searchfor'; with only kdb_grep_trailing set it returns 1 when the strlen(searchfor) bytes ending just before the trailing newline of 'searched' equal 'searchfor'; with neither flag set it returns 1 only if the length guard strlen(searched)-1 >= strlen(searchfor) has passed and 'searchfor' occurs as a substring of the null-terminated 'searched' (strchr on the first character then strncmp; the trailing newline is part of the searched text and can be matched, an empty 'searchfor' matches any non-empty 'searched'), and 0 otherwise; a 'searchfor' as long as the whole 'searched' including its newline is therefore never found.
note: Read kdb_io.c:531-559. Reviewer claims: round-1 (unanchored search includes the trailing newline) RIGHT; round-15 (searchfor equal to the whole searched text, e.g. 'x\n' in 'x\n', fails the len1 < len2 guard and returns 0) RIGHT (537-540): prose corrected. Anchored cases verified at 541-548: the trailing case compares from searched + len1 - len2, i.e. the len2 bytes before the last character.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(perf_event_open,
prose: The perf_event_open system call (core.c:13463-13870); the packet slice covered only its middle. It returns a new file descriptor (>= 0, installed with fd_install after everything succeeded) or a negative errno. Before allocating anything it returns -EINVAL for invalid flags, the error from perf_copy_attr, security_perf_event_open and the perf_allow_kernel / security_locked_down / capability checks (including -EACCES). It then allocates an unused fd (its error is returned) and from that point every failure releases what was acquired, in reverse order, through the labels err_context (put the pmu context), err_locked (unlock and unpin the context, put_ctx), err_cred (release task->signal->exec_update_lock), err_alloc (put_event), err_task (put_task_struct) and err_fd (put_unused_fd), and returns err. The failures after fd allocation include -EBADF/-ENODEV for a bad group_fd, an error from finding the task or -ESRCH, -EINVAL/-EOPNOTSUPP for invalid combinations, errors from perf_init_event, perf_event_set_clock, the interruptible exec_update_lock acquisition, context lookup, -EACCES from the ptrace-mode check, group/move-group compatibility errors (-EINVAL, -ENODEV), the pmu context allocation error, perf_event_set_output errors, -E2BIG, -EBUSY, and an error from anon_inode_getfile. On success the event is installed in its context (moving a group when requested), the context mutex and the task's exec_update_lock (if a task was given) are released, the event is added to current->perf_event_list under perf_event_mutex, and the fd is returned.
note: Packet item was an unnamed excerpt; real function is the perf_event_open syscall (core.c:13463-13870). All return and goto sites listed from a returns/gotos pass; details of each -EINVAL site were not enumerated. Old prose (holds SRCU, references released) was too thin and its SRCU precondition is not stated in this function.

name: init_hw_breakpoint
prose: Precondition: the breakpoint subsystem has not been initialized yet (constraints_initialized is false) and no other thread initializes it concurrently. Postcondition: rhltable_init is called on task_bps_ht and, if it fails, the function returns its negative error code with nothing else changed; otherwise init_breakpoint_slots is called and, if it fails, the function returns its negative error code leaving task_bps_ht initialized and constraints_initialized still false; otherwise constraints_initialized is set to true, perf_pmu_register registers the "breakpoint" PMU (its return value is ignored, so its success is not guaranteed), and the function returns the result of register_die_notifier(&hw_breakpoint_exceptions_nb), i.e. 0 on success or a negative error code on failure, in which case the hash table, the breakpoint slots, constraints_initialized and the PMU registration remain in place but the die notifier is not registered.
note: Read hw_breakpoint.c:1007-1024: matches the prose (rhltable_init error, init_breakpoint_slots error, constraints_initialized, perf_pmu_register result ignored, return of register_die_notifier). Packet name was truncated; real name is init_hw_breakpoint.
